name: Trusty
label: Dischord
lede: Trusty were a pop-punk band from Little Rock who loved Washington's scene enough to move there in 1992. Two Dischord albums later, one of them closing on a song named for the Orange Line, they packed up and went back south.

eras.title: Little Rock first
eras.text: Before Dischord, Trusty were already one of Little Rock's best-known underground bands, with records out and a national tour behind them, all from Arkansas.

years.h: Bobby Matthews starts a band in Little Rock
years.p: [[Bobby Matthews|0cec47d8-1869-44fe-b493-f79256499cc3]] and [[James Brady|d0d20648-e57e-46b4-9d1f-28fc9ce0a2d7]] on guitars and vocals, Paul Bowling on bass, Bircho Birch on drums. The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette credits Matthews with founding it.
years.xp: AllMusic lists the first line-up as Brady, Matthews, "Paul" and "Bircho"; Wikipedia gives their surnames as Bowling and Birch. Punk in Little Rock was a small world, and Trusty became one of its best-known bands fast.

years.h: A Name to Depend On, on Soma Records
years.p: The first release is a 7-inch EP, out the year the band starts.

years.h: A self-titled LP on Truant, then the road
years.p: The debut full-length comes out on Truant Records. By now, per Dischord, the band had toured the country too.

years.h: Brad Long takes over on bass from Paul Bowling
years.p: Bowling leaves. [[Brad Long|107b528c-35a8-493d-9f83-df90a95210b2]], formerly of Sobering Consequences, steps in, per AllMusic.

eras.title: Moving to the city they'd been listening to
eras.text: Dischord says several members were longtime fans of the DC scene and moved there in 1992. Wikipedia describes the years after as a slog for respect from a scene that didn't hand it out to newcomers.

years.p: Wikipedia says the next four years, 1992 to 1996, went to earning respect from the established DC punk scene.
years.xp: Dischord frames the move as fandom: several members were devoted to DC's music and relocated to be part of it. They arrived with records and national tours behind them, which in DC counted for less than showing up.

years.p: The EP is the band's first release after the move to DC.

years.h: Jim Schaffer replaces Bircho Birch on drums
years.p: AllMusic places the drum change after Cockatoo. [[Jim Schaffer|b1513e4a-6075-45f0-b86e-9b62ac9ad321]] completes the line-up that would make both Dischord albums.
The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette dates the signing to 1994. That year Truant also issues The Paul Years Retrospective, collecting the first line-up with Bowling.

eras.title: Two albums, then home
eras.text: Goodbye Dr. Fate and The Fourth Wise Man came out on Dischord and went to Europe with them. In summer 1997, with another US tour ahead, the band quit and headed south.

years.h: Goodbye Dr. Fate, a year in the making
years.p: Trusty produced their first Dischord album themselves between November 1993 and October 1994, at WGNS and Inner Ear. Fourteen songs.
years.xp: The title nods to the DC Comics sorcerer Doctor Fate, and there's a song called "Kal-el" too. Session dates are from Wikipedia; the studios from Dischord.

years.h: The Fourth Wise Man ends on the Orange Line
years.p: Trusty's second Dischord album, No. 104, recorded at Inner Ear. Twelve songs, closing with "Orange Line", named for the Metro line the band now lived on.
years.xp: Elsewhere on the record: a song titled "A Shit-Ass Scene For Nature Boy."

years.p: AllMusic dates Trusty's first European tour to 1996, the year The Fourth Wise Man came out. Dischord says they covered North America and Europe.

years.h: The band quits before a third major US tour
years.p: AllMusic says the breakup was announced in July 1997. Dischord dates the end to that summer, as members moved south.
years.xp: Other sources run later: Wikipedia and the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette both say Trusty folded in 1998, which may reflect when the last of it wound down. Dischord's summer 1997 is used here.

eras.title: Reunions, outtakes and an art class
eras.text: Trusty never stayed gone for long: a side band, a string of reunions, an outtakes record from a Little Rock label, and a formal end in 2008.

years.h: Brady and Schaffer start the Blisters
years.p: The two Trusty members form the Blisters with Kathy Cashel of [[Norman Mayer Group|4178dab8-59f4-4c04-8b99-de46a160eb87]], per AllMusic. Wikipedia lists a Trusty reunion the same year.

years.h: "Goodbye Dr. Fate" goes on Dischord's 20-year box set
years.p: The song lands on 20 Years of Dischord, Dischord No. 125.

years.h: Outtakes from a Little Rock label
years.p: Max Recordings, a Little Rock label, releases Sugar Smack, a collection of Trusty outtakes. The Arkansas Times reported the band reuniting in late 2005.

years.h: A reissued demo and a formal end
years.p: DC-Jam Records reissues Trusty's 1987 demo, recorded two years before the band's official start. AllMusic marks 2008 as the formal end.

years.h: The founder teaches art to 15 years of Memphis kids
years.p: The Democrat-Gazette reports Bobby Matthews taught elementary-school art in Memphis for 15 years. A comedy bit at a Trusty reunion show pushed him into improv, and by 2016 he co-ran a Little Rock comedy show.

sources.title: Arkansas Democrat-Gazette: Ex-punk rocker, theater director form momandpop show
